title: The Fish-basket.
note: Threats, killing and an animal death.
summary: A stolen catch becomes a contest between physical force and deception.

title: The Storm.
note: Deception and rough treatment.
summary: A storm warning gets Tiger tied to his own mango tree.

title: Tiger as Riding-horse.
note: Humiliation and a song referring to death.
summary: A boast about Tiger becomes a public demonstration.

title: Tiger’s Breakfast.
note: Food theft, bodily injury and animal cruelty.
summary: A breakfast trick is answered by a dangerous instruction.

title: The Christening.
teller: Charles Wright, Maroon Town, Cock-pit country.
note: Theft and false accusation.
summary: Names of imaginary children conceal a disappearing shared meal.

title: Tacoomah’s Corn-piece.
note: Crop theft and a death.
summary: Anansi’s music gives instructions while providing him with an alibi.

title: The Rain.
note: Threat of being eaten.
summary: A goat uses transformation and another animal’s help to escape.

title: Turtle’s Escape.
note: Threat of being cooked and eaten.
summary: Turtle turns the expected behaviour of cooking water into a route out.

title: Quit-quit and Anansi.
teller: David Roach, Lacovia. / Henry Spence, Bog, Westmoreland.
note: Rivalry, humiliation and nudity.
summary: Two versions let music, food and rivalry change who wins attention.

title: Why Tumble-bug Rolls in the Dung.
teller: William Forbes, Dry River, Cock-pit country.
note: Dung, theft and humiliation.
summary: Swapped jars turn a marriage competition into an animal explanation.

title: Why Dog is always Looking.
note: Deception about land and food.
summary: Anansi’s description of a yam harvest depends on a change of scale.

title: Why Rocks at the River are covered with Moss.
note: Injury and the removal of skin.
summary: A rock asks to share a meal, then refuses to let Anansi leave.

title: Why Toad Croaks.
note: Attempted scalding and a threat of death.
summary: Toad completes a task, but the promised reward becomes a threat.

title: Why Woodpecker Bores Wood.
teller: Samuel Wright, Maroon Town, Cock-pit country.
note: A mother’s illness, death and burial.
summary: A burial promise explains woodpecker’s work.

title: Rat’s Wedding.
teller: Thomas Williams, Harmony Hall, Cock-pit country.
note: A rat is trapped and killed; widowhood.
summary: Burnt wedding rice draws Rat away from his new wife.

title: The Fasting Trial (fragment).
note: Hunger; the source labels this a fragment.
summary: A brief fasting contest is preserved with two sets of song words.

title: Settling the Father’s Debt.
note: A dying child, parasites and household debt.
summary: A child’s riddling explanations become payment of a family debt.

title: The Tree-wife.
note: Magical marriage, nakedness and a disputed household relationship.
summary: A tree becomes a wife; a song follows a trail of answers.

title: The Barking Puppy.
teller: Alfred Williams, Maroon Town, Cock-pit country.
note: Graphic animal cruelty and a fatal violent attack.
summary: A warning survives repeated attempts to silence it.

title: The Golden Cage.
note: A child is thrown into a well; retaliatory violence.
summary: A king’s daughter and a bird’s warning song.

title: Bird Arinto.
note: A flesh-eating bird, abandonment and killing.
summary: David Lawrence defeats a bird; Anansi claims the achievement.

title: Anansi and Mosquito.
note: Betrayal and an unpaid collaborator.
summary: Mosquito learns a hidden name, but Anansi keeps the reward.

title: The Water Crayfish.
note: A child is hit; a magical child leaves a household.
summary: A found child returns to the river and reveals another identity.

title: Robin as Fortune-teller.
note: Animals killed for food and a false claim to special knowledge.
summary: Accidental remarks make Robin look like a successful fortune-teller.
